title: Kris Jenner Is the Matriarch of the Ferragamo Family in the Brand’s Holiday Campaign
text:
Kris Jenner Is the Matriarch of the Ferragamo Family in the Brand’s Holiday Campaign MENU FASHION Kris Jenner Is the Matriarch of the Ferragamo Family in the Brand’s Holiday Campaign
 Plus more of the best campaigns of the holiday season.
 by W Staff Updated:  Oct. 22, 2026 Originally Published:  Oct. 16, 2026 Courtesy of Ferragamo It is never too early to get into the holiday spirit. Everyone knows the Christmas season can be stressful, but the more you prepare ahead of time, the more you can enjoy all the magic. So while it may seem too early to start considering your gifts, in reality, you’ll just be saving your future self a lot of stress. And luckily, the brands are, once again, ahead of schedule, already rolling out their holiday content for our benefit. Ferragamo, Dior, Chanel, and more have released their 2026 holiday campaigns, and the images are getting us in the yuletide mood. So while the leaves may just now be falling off the trees, soon they’ll be on the ground, covered in snow—and there’s no time like the present to dive into the 2026 holiday campaigns.
 Ferragamo
 Photograph by Ilya Lipkin; Courtesy of Ferragamo Kris Jenner is the matriarch of the Ferragamo family in the brand’s 2026 holiday campaign, The Joy of Loving. “Ferragamo is all about family,” says creative director Maximilian Davis. “And when I design, I am always thinking about that, too: how a collection can be worn by different generations, but also how pieces you love will be held onto and passed down through them.” 
 Ferragamo
 Photograph by Ilya Lipkin; Courtesy of Ferragamo The momager stars as the director of a fictional film, leading screen tests featuring the campaign’s various faces. There’s Paloma Elsesser and her brother, Sage; girl group The Womack Sisters; and Sofia Testino with her dog, Syko. Actress Joan Chen is joined by her daughter, Audrey Hui, while acting coach Nancy Banks poses with her son, actor Benny Buckley. 
 Ferragamo
 Photograph by Ilya Lipkin; Courtesy of Ferragamo The campaign connects back to the roots of Ferragamo, and founder Salvatore Ferragamo’s original desire to build a better life for his family through his love of invention and creativity. “One of the founding values of Ferragamo has always been of beauty that develops from craftsmanship, humanity, and joy,” says Salvatore’s son, Leonardo Ferragamo. “This campaign is telling that story.” 
 Loro Piana
 Photograph by Annemarieke Van Drimmelen; Courtesy of Loro Piana Loro Piana invites you to a weekend at the cabin, where the elegantly falling snow outside matches the chic inhabitants’ wardrobes. Models are dressed in the brand’s holiday collection, an expression of style that plays out across textures, hand-finished prints, exclusive patterns, and elaborate stitches. 
 Loro Piana 
 Photograph by Annemarieke Van Drimmelen; Courtesy of Loro Piana Loro Piana’s usually muted color palette is realized once again, this time in the form of dark greens and earthy browns. They are highlighted with pops of winter-white and marigold. 
 Loro Piana
 Photograph by Annemarieke Van Drimmelen; Courtesy of Loro Piana Warm jersey tops and trousers form the foundations of these après-ski looks. On top, classic Loro Piana outerwear like the Spagna jacket and Konny vest are crafted in wool and finely detailed with needlework; the wearer stays warm while also making an enviable sartorial impression. 
 Chanel
 Courtesy of Chanel Chanel is hitting the slopes for its 2026 Coco Neige collection. Bright-red knits and colorblocked puffers stand out against snow-capped mountains. The images have a retro flair, but the clothing is distinctly modern. 
 Chanel
 Courtesy of Chanel A snowball fight adds even more joy to this already playful campaign, while penguin and polar bear-shaped purses and earrings provide the perfect amount of whimsy. 
 Chanel
 Courtesy of Chanel Shearling caps keep ears warm, while winter whites are embraced with aplomb. It’s a reminder that dressing for warmth does not mean sacrificing style or charm. 
 Dior
 Indulge in your sweet tooth with Dior’s 2026 holiday campaign, which sees the brand’s famous 30 Montaigne store reimagined as a sugar-dusted gingerbread house. Anya Taylor-Joy and Deva Cassel star in a joyous musical video. The house’s ambassadors prance around the store, snacking on Dior cookies, spritzing the brand’s famed fragrances, and trimming the icing-lined cookie Christmas tree. 
 This article was originally published on Oct. 16, 2026
